reviews.comment: I took Dr. Lei for Modern Chinese Fiction, and while there were a lot of readings, I enjoyed the class discussions and her lectures. She's great at giving feedback on essays, and you always know exactly where you stand with her. She'll work with you quite a bit. Would definitely recommend taking her classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I have never had to put in as much effort into an elective as I did for this class. She's extremely stingy with her grading, and always seemed to improvise for class, which was really annoying since attendance was mandatory. On top of that, a 10 page paper for the final. This class made me consider dropping my minor and I'm so glad its over.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was the most disorganized class with the most incompetent professor I've had in my life. For a class with such an emphasis on writing, you will get basically no rubric or clear grading criteria. Essay feedback says so many words yet nothing at once. Will put in grade and then lower it an hour later with no explanation. 0/10
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Lei is really caring and does want to see students succeed. There is a lot of reading outside of class, but she breaks it down well during class for discussions. Expect a lot of writing, a presentation, and a paper. However, she guides students through these assignments quite well, she really cares about the effort students make in class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Lei is an amazing prof. Lectures are insightful, fair grader & gives great feedback. HW consists of reading 1 chapter each of 2 textbooks per week & answering 2 SAQs & a 10-page research paper as your final assignment. Don't be daunted, she walks you through the whole process of finding a topic, writing, etc. Loved her class, 100% would retake.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Ill be honest, this is a very difficult class. However, professor Lei is a very passionate teacher and she genuinely just wants to see her students succeed. Theres lots of reading so I suggest connecting with other students to discuss the concepts. Dont be daunted, I promise that she doesnt grade harshly and just wants to see an effort.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jun Lei i is definitely a difficult professor. She will make you work for your grade and lectures are pretty much entirely in Chinese. While she is strict, she is also a caring professor. My recommendation is to take this class if you are dedicated to learning Chinese and go to class! Sit in the front and participate often. That is how to get an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unclear standards, drowns out your opinion with her own. If you don't agree with social matters with her exactly, good luck passing the class. And when she is about to fail you because your opinions differ, she is non-committal on confrontation and being clear with you.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was always prepared for class. The schedule was always clear when we had tests and quizzes. She made class fun by keeping us entertained & involved. If you show up to office hours she is extremely helpful, and she really just cares about us learning Chinese. She will push you and make you work for it, so put in the effort and you'll do great.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's an engaging, personable, and challenging language teacher. You won't be bored in her class because she's funny and always finds entertaining ways to practice what we're learning. She cares a lot about her students' experiences so she consistently asks how she can improve her teaching style. She's tough, but in the way that ensures you learn.

I will give her a little bit of slack since she is a new professor, straight out of graduate school. This (Mandarin) Chinese class is designed for non-native speakers. However, she grades like if we were native speakers.  There were also words  that showed up on quizzes and tests that we have never seen the two characters together.
